statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 14% sits in the low band, below the 20% watch threshold and well below the 25% block level.
recommendation: Tail remains below both the watch and block thresholds. The Nasdaq-100 set a record intraday high at 31,361.37 and then closed 0.44% lower at 31,224.47, just above its session low, so the retracement off the high was granted and extended rather than failing. VIX closed near its session low at 14.99 and both the 10-year and 30-year yields eased, so the observed structure is an orderly session in which mean reversion is functioning. Stress stays elevated at 45% on the 30-year yield near 5.64%, Brent near $100, record three-stock index concentration above 21% of the S&P 500, and narrow leadership, but none of that has produced the shallow-pullback or failed-retracement signature that defines Tail. The narrow danger window is limited to the 10-year note auction and FOMC minutes block between 17:00Z and 19:00Z on 7 October. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
headline: Nasdaq-100 fades 0.44% off a 31,361.37 record high to close at 31,224.47 near the session low as VIX and yields ease; Tail eases to 14% with the FOMC minutes block the next checkpoint
body: The Nasdaq-100 ended the 6 October US cash session at 31,224.47, up 148.03 points or 0.48%, having set a 31,361.37 record intraday high earlier in the day. The close is the decisive observation of this hour: price finished 0.44% below that high and only 16.27 points above the 31,208.20 session low, so the retracement off the record was granted and then extended into the bell. That is the signature of functioning mean reversion, not of a pathological no-retracement path. The session low still held 0.42% above Monday's 31,076.44 record close, so the gap above the prior record is unfilled and the uptrend remains structurally intact on a daily basis, which is why the dominant mode is read as mixed rather than trend-up: an intact daily uptrend combined with an observed two-way close. December NQ futures continue price discovery at 31,499.50, up 0.58%, roughly 0.37% below their own 31,616.50 session high inside a 31,309.25-31,616.50 range. Cross-asset evidence de-amplifies rather than confirms. VIX closed at 14.99, down 3.41%, at the low end of a 14.96-15.54 range against a 15.52 previous close. The 10-year yield eased four basis points to 5.27% within a 5.26-5.30% range after Monday's 5.31% close, the highest in 24 years, and the 30-year eased to 5.64% from 5.66%. Semiconductors tracked the index down off the highs rather than leading away from it: the SOX finished at 13,217.82, up 0.34%, near its 13,196.50 low and 0.99% under its 13,349.96 session high. The broader tape was firm, with the S&P 500 at 7,818.93 (+0.58%) at a record, the Nasdaq Composite at 27,599.79 (+0.45%) for a back-to-back record close, and the Dow at 51,521.28 (+0.49%). Standing fragilities keep Stress elevated without supporting Tail. Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft together exceed 21% of the S&P 500, the most concentrated three-stock weighting on record, leaving the benchmark dependent on very few names. Nvidia and AMD both touched fresh record highs with Nvidia's market capitalisation approaching $6 trillion, Marvell gained roughly 8% after raising fiscal 2028 revenue guidance to about $20 billion, and Constellation Energy rose about 13% on a $4.3 billion twenty-year nuclear supply agreement with Google. Leadership therefore remains narrow. Energy is the clearest conflicting input: WTI is $89.85, up 0.47%, after a wide $86.86-$90.05 range, and Brent trades near $100, elevated but two-way rather than breaking out. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 2026-09-29 with a partial collection status, far outside its 90-minute freshness contract, so it was not used; that failure is isolated and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified current sources, which is what Confidence is scored on. The forward window carries two genuine scheduled checkpoints on 7 October: the 10-year note auction at 17:00Z, which matters precisely because the long end has only just eased from a 24-year-high close, and the FOMC minutes at 18:00Z, a structurally multi-stage event whose headline read, yield reaction and delayed equity second leg can separate. Those two hours define the narrow danger window. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with forecast Tail peaking at 23% in the minutes hour, inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail ran 17% at 20:00Z on 5 October, fell through the overnight hours to a low of 8% at 05:00Z as the index mean-reverted in thin liquidity, then rebuilt with the European and US sessions to a 22% peak at 15:00Z on 6 October around the record-high push. The final hours settled back to 17-18% as the retracement off the high was granted and held. Dominant mode ran trend-up at the start of the window, moved to mixed overnight, and returned to trend-up from 10:00Z through the US session. Stress stayed in the elevated band throughout, between 45% and 51%, and Confidence held in the high band between 86% and 88%.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to ease through the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins, reaching a 9% trough between 04:00Z and 05:00Z. It rebuilds with the European open and the US pre-market, then rises into the 7 October US session: 19% for the cash-open hour at 13:00Z, 20-21% through the EIA and Consumer Inflation Expectations hours, 22% for the 17:00Z 10-year note auction, and a 23% peak in the 18:00Z FOMC minutes hour. That peak stays inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold because no pathological price path is observed; it reflects the aligned catalyst stack of a 10-year auction and multi-stage minutes landing with the long end near multi-decade highs. Stress follows the same arc from 43% overnight to 52% at the minutes, and Confidence decays from 87% to 81% as live cash evidence ages.
